top_news.title: Vietnam: Free Abducted Democracy Group Activists
top_news.summary: Click to expand Image Tran Hiep. Private (Bangkok) - TheVietnamese authorities should immediately release three activists associated with the overseas Viet Tan organization who went missing in Cambodia, and drop all charges against them, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should also grant Norwegian and Australian consular officials and family members immediate access to the detained men. The Vietnamese policeclaim that Nguyen Duc Thuan, a Norwegian citizen; Tran Hiep (also known as Ho Pham Hiep Huy), an Australian citizen; and Thai Cong Truong Son are members of the outlawed Viet Tan organization and attempted to use fake documents to cross the border from Cambodia to Vietnam on September 18, 2026. The men's relatives say they never attempted to enter Vietnam. The police announced that they have charged the three men with terrorism under article 299 of the penal code for their association with Viet Tan and with forgery of seals and documents under article 341. Viet Tan is an overseas political organization that advocates for democratic change in Vietnam. It contends that the men were abducted in Cambodia. The apparent abduction and detention of the foreign nationals raises many questions about the roles of both the Vietnamese and Cambodian governments, saidElaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. The Norwegian and Australian governments should press the Vietnamese authorities to grant them immediate access to their nationals and to drop baseless charges against them. Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep flew to Phnom Penh on September 15 and werereportedly in regular contact withfamily members outside of Cambodia until the morning of September 18, after which neither could be reached. Both men missed other scheduled appointments in Cambodia and the flight they had booked to leave Cambodia on September 19; they have not been heard from since. Their luggage and other effects except phones and passports were found in their hotel rooms in Cambodia. Nguyen Duc Thuan requires daily insulin injections for diabetes and medical attention for kidney problems. As of October 11, neither the Australian nor Norwegian embassy had been granted access to the detained men. The Vietnamese policeclaimed that the three men crossed the border into Vietnam at Tay Ninh province, and that Nguyen Duc Thuan was carrying two fake Vietnamese citizen identification cards under a fake name and a Norwegian passport under his real name. They said that Ho Pham Hiep Huy was carrying an Australian passport in the name of Tran Hiep. The police statement does not describe Thai Cong Truong Son's identification. On October 7, Cambodia's Ministry of Interiorissued a statement saying it had confirmed that Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep had entered Cambodia but had not recorded their exit. And said it categorically denied any involvement in handing over the men to the Vietnamese authorities. In the 1980s, Viet Tan had engaged in armed resistance against Vietnam's communist government. Viet Tan relaunched in 2004 as a political party committed to nonviolent change, but the Vietnamese authorities have arrested and imprisoned Viet Tan members. In 2016, Vietnam officially labeled Viet Tan a terrorist group. In 2019, an Australian member of Viet Tan,Chau Van Kham, and his colleagues Nguyen Van Vien and Tran Van Quyen were arrested in Vietnam and sentenced to 12, 11, and 10 years, respectively, for their involvement with Viet Tan on terrorism-related charges. Their trial lasted only 4.5 hours, suggesting that the verdict was pre-determined. The activities listed in the government's charges against Chau Van Kham and attributed to Viet Tan, such as making travel arrangements to Vietnam, organizing leaflets for protests, expanding the Viet Tan's network, writing articles, and sending people abroad for IT training, do not constitute acts of terrorism. In 2022, the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention issued anopinion stating that the deprivation of liberty of [Viet Tan member] Chau Van Kham ... isarbitrary. Vietnam released Chau Van Kham in July 2023 and repatriated him to Australia. His Vietnamese fellow activists Nguyen Van Vien and Tran Van Quyen are still serving long prison sentences. In 2018, the Vietnamese police arrested Le Quoc Binh in Binh Dinh province andaccused him of participating in Viet Tan and smuggling weapons from Cambodia into Vietnam to carry out terrorist activities. Viet Tanrejected the accusation, calling it a ridiculous fabrication. The then-public security minister and current Vietnamese president, To Lam,praised the police for arresting Le Quoc Binh. Later accounts in government media of his trial and conviction on charges of terrorism and illegal possession of weaponsdropped all mention of Viet Tan. In May 2026, the Vietnamese police arrestedLe Thanh Son and Nguyen Thanh Hung in Dong Thap province for their alleged affiliation with Viet Tan and charged them with carrying out activities that aim to overthrow the people's administration under article 109 of the penal code. Also in May, the policereportedly detained, interrogated and beat aformer political prisoner, Huynh Truong Ca, and forced him to admit that he was a member of Viet Tan, which he denied. After Huynh Truong Ca fled, police detained his family members, interrogated them on his whereabouts, and intimidated and pressured them to denounce him. In recent years, the Vietnamese authorities have stepped up transnational repression-government efforts to silence dissent by targeting dissidents and critics outside their territory. They have pressured other governments, includingThailand andCambodia, to return Vietnamese citizens who fled Vietnam out of fear of arbitrary arrest, torture, or imprisonment. Vietnamese security forces have abducted Vietnamese citizens in Germany and Thailand, includingTrinh Xuan Thanh, Truong Duy Nhat, and Duong Van Thai. In the past year, courts in Vietnam put on trial in absentia Vietnamese nationals who live overseas, convicting and sentencing them to long prison terms, includingLe Trung Khoa, Nguyen Van Dai, Doan Bao Chau, Dinh Yum, Siu Di, andDang Thi Hue. Since the trials, the police have issued numerous warnings and fined Vietnamese citizens for interacting with those convicted in absentia. Activists from Vietnam and Thailand have been forciblydisappeared in Cambodia in cases of suspected transnational repression. Campaigning for democracy and pluralism is not a crime, Pearson said. The Vietnamese government should release Nguyen Duc Thuan, Tran Hiep, and Thai Cong Truong Son and end its practice of transnational repression.

top_news.title: BIMSTEC Ministerial declaration calls for unified stand against cross-border terrorism, cybercrime, and human trafficking
top_news.summary: Home Ministers of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation member countries have adopted a comprehensive joint declaration prioritising robust, coordinated measures against evolving regional security threats, following the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi on Tuesday. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), the joint declaration "emphasised combating cross-border terrorism, terror financing, radicalisation, drug trafficking, human trafficking, cybercrime, and organised crime." The ministry stated that the framework "prioritised information sharing, mutual legal assistance, extradition, capacity building, and the effective implementation of existing agreements and plans of action," while placing special stress on "the protection of victims of human trafficking involved in online scams." To strengthen the regional security framework, Home Ministers of the BIMSTEC member states formally approved five key agreements and action plans during the meeting. The BIMSTEC Convention against Trafficking in Persons was approved to enhance regional cooperation among member states in preventing human trafficking, criminalising the offence, and ensuring the protection and rehabilitation of victims. The BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Drug Control was adopted to combat the illicit trafficking of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, and precursor chemicals across borders. Ministers approved a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Capacity Building among BIMSTEC Countries to Combat Money Laundering and Terror Financing. This agreement provides for the training of experts, the exchange of best practices, and extensive cooperation across financial crimes, financial intelligence, investigations, asset recovery, anti-money laundering measures, countering the financing of terrorism, and countering proliferation financing. The BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Illicit Financial Flows and Their Prevention was endorsed to identify the sources, risks, and channels of illicit financial movements among member countries. Additionally, ministers agreed on a Plan of Action for Enhancing Preparedness and Coordination to Address Natural Disasters in the Bay of Bengal Region. This initiative proposes coordinated efforts in regional risk planning, joint exercises, early warning systems, disaster mapping, training centres, information sharing, research, technological innovation, and tsunami risk reduction. Highlighting India's pivotal role in steering the regional security framework, the MHA noted that the declaration "appreciated India's leadership in strengthening regional security cooperation." In response, New Delhi reaffirmed its commitment to providing institutional support and expertise to member nations. "India reiterated its commitment to sharing its expertise in police training, counter-terrorism operations, and forensic investigations," the MHA stated. The ministry further highlighted that "the meeting also emphasised cooperation in disaster management, including the proposed BIMSTEC Centre for Disaster Management in Jamnagar, Gujarat." Describing the outcome of the ministerial gathering as a major milestone for Bay of Bengal regional stability, the Ministry of Home Affairs emphasised that "this meeting was an important step towards making the BIMSTEC region safer and more prosperous." Following the meeting, Home Minister Amit Shah met with his Nepali counterpart Sudhan Gurung. Highlighting their discussion, the Nepal Embassy in India wrote in a post on X that HM Gurung expressed gratitude towards India's timely assistance following the flash floods that ravaged Kathmandu in August. "Home Minister Sudhan Gurung met with Amit Shah, Union Home Minister of India, on the sidelines of the First BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi today. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral security cooperation, coordination on border management, combating transnational crime, and enhancing disaster preparedness and response. Hon. Minister Gurung expressed appreciation for India's timely assistance following the recent floods and landslides in Nepal and emphasised advancing practical cooperation for the mutual benefit of both peoples, guided by sovereign equality, mutual respect and trust," the Embassy wrote. https

top_news.title: "We are sharing intel" with Ukraine: Trump says US helping Kyiv, Moscow to end war
top_news.summary: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) said that Washington was continuing to share intelligence with Ukraine and was working with both Kyiv and Moscow to end the Russia-Ukraine war, adding that both sides wanted the conflict to end but did not know how to reach that point. Addressing reporters before departing for a campaign in Alaska, Trump denied that the United States had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine. No, we haven't. We help them. But we're really hoping to get to a final answer. We want the war ended, Peter. We are helping them, and we are sharing Intel. We want the war to end. So, we're working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end, Trump said. When asked what gave him confidence that Russian President Vladimir Putin wanted to end the war more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump said his experience in negotiations informed his assessment. Only in dealing, that's what I've done my whole life is deals. I think Putin wants it probably... They both want it to end, and they don't know how to get to that point. There's a lot of hatred there between the two of them. We're going to get them there, he said. On concerns raised by some Republican senators over the diesel deal involving Russia, Trump said the arrangement was intended to supply the global market rather than the United States, arguing that the move would help address high energy prices. Nobody told me anything. That's a diesel deal, not for us. That's being released into the world. That's not being released to us. That's a diesel deal that's going to be released into the world for the world market. Because the world market suffers from high prices. And when you knock out diesel refineries, that's not a great thing, Trump said. When a reporter cited Russia's strikes on energy sites in Ukraine on Monday, Trump responded by pointing to Ukrainian strikes on the preceding day. Well, Ukraine hit many sites the day before, he said. Asked whether Russia had violated the energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv, Trump declined to give an immediate assessment. I'll let you know about that later, he said. But they're hitting each other. But it'll all come to an end, Trump added. Trump had earlier said Russia would supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel, followed by another 500,000 tonnes during November and one million tonnes immediately thereafter, with a further three million tonnes expected within a short period depending on the condition of Russian diesel refineries. Russian President Vladimir Putin had also said that proposed Russian oil and petroleum product supplies to the United States and global markets would positively affect the global economy. According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, the issue was discussed during a telephone conversation between Putin and Trump on Friday, which also covered Ukraine and Iran. His remarks come as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday accused Russia of ignoring the call by US President Donald Trump's call for an energy ceasefire, after Moscow launched heavy strikes across Ukraine despite Kyiv honouring a pause on targeting Russian energy assets. Ukraine has not carried out strikes on Russian oil refineries or the energy sector in general for the two days since the American President announced an energy ceasefire. But Russia did not heed the American President, Zelenskyy said in a post on X. According to the Ukrainian President, Russian forces launched over a hundred weapons, including jet-powered drones, loitering munitions, and ballistic missiles, from last evening through today. While Ukrainian forces intercepted a significant portion of these strike assets, several hit civilian and critical infrastructure across 19 Ukrainian regions in just two days. Trump had claimed that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to reach a deal to end the Russia-Ukraine war more than Zelenskyy, while reiterating that both leaders must come together to end the conflict amid questions over alleged violations of the proposed energy ceasefire. (ANI)

articles.title: Vietnam: Free Abducted Democracy Group Activists
articles.summary: Click to expand Image Tran Hiep. Private (Bangkok) - TheVietnamese authorities should immediately release three activists associated with the overseas Viet Tan organization who went missing in Cambodia, and drop all charges against them, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should also grant Norwegian and Australian consular officials and family members immediate access to the detained men. The Vietnamese policeclaim that Nguyen Duc Thuan, a Norwegian citizen; Tran Hiep (also known as Ho Pham Hiep Huy), an Australian citizen; and Thai Cong Truong Son are members of the outlawed Viet Tan organization and attempted to use fake documents to cross the border from Cambodia to Vietnam on September 18, 2026. The men's relatives say they never attempted to enter Vietnam. The police announced that they have charged the three men with terrorism under article 299 of the penal code for their association with Viet Tan and with forgery of seals and documents under article 341. Viet Tan is an overseas political organization that advocates for democratic change in Vietnam. It contends that the men were abducted in Cambodia. The apparent abduction and detention of the foreign nationals raises many questions about the roles of both the Vietnamese and Cambodian governments, saidElaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. The Norwegian and Australian governments should press the Vietnamese authorities to grant them immediate access to their nationals and to drop baseless charges against them. Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep flew to Phnom Penh on September 15 and werereportedly in regular contact withfamily members outside of Cambodia until the morning of September 18, after which neither could be reached. Both men missed other scheduled appointments in Cambodia and the flight they had booked to leave Cambodia on September 19; they have not been heard from since. Their luggage and other effects except phones and passports were found in their hotel rooms in Cambodia. Nguyen Duc Thuan requires daily insulin injections for diabetes and medical attention for kidney problems. As of October 11, neither the Australian nor Norwegian embassy had been granted access to the detained men. The Vietnamese policeclaimed that the three men crossed the border into Vietnam at Tay Ninh province, and that Nguyen Duc Thuan was carrying two fake Vietnamese citizen identification cards under a fake name and a Norwegian passport under his real name. They said that Ho Pham Hiep Huy was carrying an Australian passport in the name of Tran Hiep. The police statement does not describe Thai Cong Truong Son's identification. On October 7, Cambodia's Ministry of Interiorissued a statement saying it had confirmed that Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep had entered Cambodia but had not recorded their exit. And said it categorically denied any involvement in handing over the men to the Vietnamese authorities. In the 1980s, Viet Tan had engaged in armed resistance against Vietnam's communist government. Viet Tan relaunched in 2004 as a political party committed to nonviolent change, but the Vietnamese authorities have arrested and imprisoned Viet Tan members. In 2016, Vietnam officially labeled Viet Tan a terrorist group. In 2019, an Australian member of Viet Tan,Chau Van Kham, and his colleagues Nguyen Van Vien and Tran Van Quyen were arrested in Vietnam and sentenced to 12, 11, and 10 years, respectively, for their involvement with Viet Tan on terrorism-related charges. Their trial lasted only 4.5 hours, suggesting that the verdict was pre-determined. The activities listed in the government's charges against Chau Van Kham and attributed to Viet Tan, such as making travel arrangements to Vietnam, organizing leaflets for protests, expanding the Viet Tan's network, writing articles, and sending people abroad for IT training, do not constitute acts of terrorism. In 2022, the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention issued anopinion stating that the deprivation of liberty of [Viet Tan member] Chau Van Kham ... isarbitrary. Vietnam released Chau Van Kham in July 2023 and repatriated him to Australia. His Vietnamese fellow activists Nguyen Van Vien and Tran Van Quyen are still serving long prison sentences. In 2018, the Vietnamese police arrested Le Quoc Binh in Binh Dinh province andaccused him of participating in Viet Tan and smuggling weapons from Cambodia into Vietnam to carry out terrorist activities. Viet Tanrejected the accusation, calling it a ridiculous fabrication. The then-public security minister and current Vietnamese president, To Lam,praised the police for arresting Le Quoc Binh. Later accounts in government media of his trial and conviction on charges of terrorism and illegal possession of weaponsdropped all mention of Viet Tan. In May 2026, the Vietnamese police arrestedLe Thanh Son and Nguyen Thanh Hung in Dong Thap province for their alleged affiliation with Viet Tan and charged them with carrying out activities that aim to overthrow the people's administration under article 109 of the penal code. Also in May, the policereportedly detained, interrogated and beat aformer political prisoner, Huynh Truong Ca, and forced him to admit that he was a member of Viet Tan, which he denied. After Huynh Truong Ca fled, police detained his family members, interrogated them on his whereabouts, and intimidated and pressured them to denounce him. In recent years, the Vietnamese authorities have stepped up transnational repression-government efforts to silence dissent by targeting dissidents and critics outside their territory. They have pressured other governments, includingThailand andCambodia, to return Vietnamese citizens who fled Vietnam out of fear of arbitrary arrest, torture, or imprisonment. Vietnamese security forces have abducted Vietnamese citizens in Germany and Thailand, includingTrinh Xuan Thanh, Truong Duy Nhat, and Duong Van Thai. In the past year, courts in Vietnam put on trial in absentia Vietnamese nationals who live overseas, convicting and sentencing them to long prison terms, includingLe Trung Khoa, Nguyen Van Dai, Doan Bao Chau, Dinh Yum, Siu Di, andDang Thi Hue. Since the trials, the police have issued numerous warnings and fined Vietnamese citizens for interacting with those convicted in absentia. Activists from Vietnam and Thailand have been forciblydisappeared in Cambodia in cases of suspected transnational repression. Campaigning for democracy and pluralism is not a crime, Pearson said. The Vietnamese government should release Nguyen Duc Thuan, Tran Hiep, and Thai Cong Truong Son and end its practice of transnational repression.

articles.title: BIMSTEC Ministerial declaration calls for unified stand against cross-border terrorism, cybercrime, and human trafficking
articles.summary: Home Ministers of the Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation member countries have adopted a comprehensive joint declaration prioritising robust, coordinated measures against evolving regional security threats, following the first BIMSTEC Home Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi on Tuesday. According to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), the joint declaration "emphasised combating cross-border terrorism, terror financing, radicalisation, drug trafficking, human trafficking, cybercrime, and organised crime." The ministry stated that the framework "prioritised information sharing, mutual legal assistance, extradition, capacity building, and the effective implementation of existing agreements and plans of action," while placing special stress on "the protection of victims of human trafficking involved in online scams." To strengthen the regional security framework, Home Ministers of the BIMSTEC member states formally approved five key agreements and action plans during the meeting. The BIMSTEC Convention against Trafficking in Persons was approved to enhance regional cooperation among member states in preventing human trafficking, criminalising the offence, and ensuring the protection and rehabilitation of victims. The BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Drug Control was adopted to combat the illicit trafficking of narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, and precursor chemicals across borders. Ministers approved a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on Capacity Building among BIMSTEC Countries to Combat Money Laundering and Terror Financing. This agreement provides for the training of experts, the exchange of best practices, and extensive cooperation across financial crimes, financial intelligence, investigations, asset recovery, anti-money laundering measures, countering the financing of terrorism, and countering proliferation financing. The BIMSTEC Plan of Action on Illicit Financial Flows and Their Prevention was endorsed to identify the sources, risks, and channels of illicit financial movements among member countries. Additionally, ministers agreed on a Plan of Action for Enhancing Preparedness and Coordination to Address Natural Disasters in the Bay of Bengal Region. This initiative proposes coordinated efforts in regional risk planning, joint exercises, early warning systems, disaster mapping, training centres, information sharing, research, technological innovation, and tsunami risk reduction. Highlighting India's pivotal role in steering the regional security framework, the MHA noted that the declaration "appreciated India's leadership in strengthening regional security cooperation." In response, New Delhi reaffirmed its commitment to providing institutional support and expertise to member nations. The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral security cooperation, coordination on border management, combating transnational crime, and enhancing disaster preparedness and response. Hon. articles.title: "We are sharing intel" with Ukraine: Trump says US helping Kyiv, Moscow to end war
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday (local time) said that Washington was continuing to share intelligence with Ukraine and was working with both Kyiv and Moscow to end the Russia-Ukraine war, adding that both sides wanted the conflict to end but did not know how to reach that point. Addressing reporters before departing for a campaign in Alaska, Trump denied that the United States had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine. No, we haven't. We help them. But we're really hoping to get to a final answer. We want the war ended, Peter. We are helping them, and we are sharing Intel. We want the war to end. So, we're working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end, Trump said. When asked what gave him confidence that Russian President Vladimir Putin wanted to end the war more than Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Trump said his experience in negotiations informed his assessment. Only in dealing, that's what I've done my whole life is deals. I think Putin wants it probably... They both want it to end, and they don't know how to get to that point. There's a lot of hatred there between the two of them. We're going to get them there, he said. On concerns raised by some Republican senators over the diesel deal involving Russia, Trump said the arrangement was intended to supply the global market rather than the United States, arguing that the move would help address high energy prices. Nobody told me anything. That's a diesel deal, not for us. That's being released into the world. That's not being released to us. That's a diesel deal that's going to be released into the world for the world market. Because the world market suffers from high prices. And when you knock out diesel refineries, that's not a great thing, Trump said. When a reporter cited Russia's strikes on energy sites in Ukraine on Monday, Trump responded by pointing to Ukrainian strikes on the preceding day. Well, Ukraine hit many sites the day before, he said. Asked whether Russia had violated the energy ceasefire between Moscow and Kyiv, Trump declined to give an immediate assessment. I'll let you know about that later, he said. But they're hitting each other. But it'll all come to an end, Trump added. Trump had earlier said Russia would supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel fuel, followed by another 500,000 tonnes during November and one million tonnes immediately thereafter, with a further three million tonnes expected within a short period depending on the condition of Russian diesel refineries. Russian President Vladimir Putin had also said that proposed Russian oil and petroleum product supplies to the United States and global markets would positively affect the global economy. According to the Russian Foreign Ministry, the issue was discussed during a telephone conversation between Putin and Trump on Friday, which also covered Ukraine and Iran. His remarks come as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Tuesday accused Russia of ignoring the call by US President Donald Trump's call for an energy ceasefire, after Moscow launched heavy strikes across Ukraine despite Kyiv honouring a pause on targeting Russian energy assets. Ukraine has not carried out strikes on Russian oil refineries or the energy sector in general for the two days since the American President announced an energy ceasefire. But Russia did not heed the American President, Zelenskyy said in a post on X. According to the Ukrainian President, Russian forces launched over a hundred weapons, including jet-powered drones, loitering munitions, and ballistic missiles, from last evening through today. While Ukrainian forces intercepted a significant portion of these strike assets, several hit civilian and critical infrastructure across 19 Ukrainian regions in just two days. Trump had claimed that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to reach a deal to end the Russia-Ukraine war more than Zelenskyy, while reiterating that both leaders must come together to end the conflict amid questions over alleged violations of the proposed energy ceasefire. (ANI)
